record.original_question: If F (z), G(z) are convex functions in Σ, it is known that for 0 < λ < 1, H(z) = λF (z) + (1 − λ)G(z) ∈ Σ, see Pommerenke [646]. Is it true that H(z) is also convex? (Ch. Pommerenke)

evidence.quote: If F (z), G(z) are convex functions in Σ, it is known that for 0 < λ < 1, H(z) = λF (z) + (1 − λ)G(z) ∈ Σ, see Pommerenke [646]. Is it true that H(z) is also convex? (Ch. Pommerenke)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ denote the class of functions $F$ that are meromorphic and univalent in the exterior of the closed unit disk $\Delta^* = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| > 1\}$ and have a Laurent expansion of the form
$$F(z) = z + b_0 + \frac{b_1}{z} + \frac{b_2}{z^2} + \cdots, \qquad |z|>1.$$
Such a function $F \in \Sigma$ is said to be convex (in $\Sigma$) if its image $F(\Delta^*)$ is the complement (in the Riemann sphere) of a bounded convex set; equivalently, $\mathbb{C}\setminus F(\Delta^*)$ is a convex compact subset of $\mathbb{C}$.

It is known that if $F, G \in \Sigma$ are both convex and $0 < \lambda < 1$, then the function
$$H(z) = \lambda F(z) + (1-\lambda) G(z)$$
again belongs to $\Sigma$ (i.e., $H$ is meromorphic and univalent on $\Delta^*$ with the appropriate normalization).

Question: Is $H(z) = \lambda F(z) + (1-\lambda) G(z)$ also convex in the above sense, for every pair of convex functions $F, G \in \Sigma$ and every $\lambda \in (0,1)$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for this convex-combination question for convex functions in the meromorphic class $\Sigma$ did not turn up an explicit resolution. Surveys on convex combinations of univalent functions and Pommerenke's monograph discuss the analogous problem in the disk class, but no source clearly states that the question for $\Sigma$ has been settled either way. The current status is therefore unclear from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: A survey of properties of the convex combination of univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey by D. M. Campbell on convex combinations of univalent functions.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys related results but does not record a resolution of the Σ-version of the problem.

status_evidence.title: Pommerenke, Univalent Functions (1975)
status_evidence.snippet: Pommerenke's standard reference on univalent functions including the class Σ.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that convex combinations of convex functions stay in Σ, but the convexity of the combination is not asserted.
